ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline — Counsel Markup of Counterparty Draft)
================================================================================
Document Status: COUNSEL REDLINE (All Required Modifications Incorporated)
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper
Parties (as corrected):
  • Debtor / Account Holder: [Borrower], a [State] [entity type] (“Company”)
  • Secured Party: [Administrative Agent], as Administrative Agent for the Lenders
    under the Credit Agreement (“Secured Party” or “Agent”)
  • Depository Bank: [Bank Name], N.A. (“Bank”)
Account(s): See Schedule A (as corrected)
Governing Law (as corrected): State of New York; UCC Article 9 control under NY UCC §§ 9-104, 9-106, 9-314
Credit Agreement Reference: Credit Agreement dated as of [CA Date] among Company, the Lenders party thereto, and Agent (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Credit Agreement”)
Playbook / Bank Form / CA Cross-Check: Internal ACA Playbook v4.2; Bank Standard Form ACA (latest); Executed Credit Agreement §§ 5.11, 6.12, 8.01, Collateral Documents definition; Account Opening Checklist; Counsel Correspondence re: springing control and NOEC mechanics

LEGEND (Tracked Changes Convention Used in This Deliverable):
  [DELETE: text]     = deletion from counterparty draft
  [INSERT: text]     = insertion required by playbook / CA / bank form / market
  [MOVE: …]          = relocation
  [COMMENT: …]       = drafting note (not contractual text)
  **ACCEPT / REJECT / COUNTER** annotations appear in the companion Issues/Risk Memo

================================================================================
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
================================================================================

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), dated as of [●], 20[●] (the “Effective Date”), is entered into by and among:

(i)  [FULL LEGAL NAME OF BORROWER], a [State] [corporation / limited liability company] (the “Company”);

(ii) [FULL LEGAL NAME OF ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT], as Administrative Agent for the benefit of the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement referred to below (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns in such capacity, the “Secured Party”); and

(iii) [FULL LEGAL NAME OF DEPOSITORY BANK], N.A. (the “Bank”).

[INSERT: The Secured Party is entering into this Agreement in its capacity as Administrative Agent under the Credit Agreement and for the ratable benefit of the Secured Parties (as defined in the Credit Agreement).]

RECITALS

A.  [DELETE: The Company maintains certain deposit accounts with the Bank.]
    [INSERT: Pursuant to that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of [CA Date] (as amended, restated, amended and restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Credit Agreement”), among the Company, the lenders from time to time party thereto (the “Lenders”), and the Secured Party, as Administrative Agent, the Lenders have agreed to extend credit to the Company on the terms and conditions set forth therein.]

B.  [INSERT: As a condition to the obligations of the Lenders under the Credit Agreement, and pursuant to the Guarantee and Collateral Agreement dated as of [GCA Date] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Security Agreement”) and the other Collateral Documents, the Company has granted (or is concurrently granting) to the Secured Party, for the benefit of the Secured Parties, a security interest in, among other things, the Account (as defined below) and all cash, checks, wire transfers, automated clearing house entries, and other items and funds from time to time on deposit in or credited to the Account (collectively, the “Account Collateral”).]

C.  [DELETE: The parties desire to enter into this agreement regarding the account.]
    [INSERT: The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party’s security interest in the Account and Account Collateral by “control” within the meaning of Sections 9-104 and 9-314 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the “UCC”), and to set forth their respective rights and obligations with respect thereto.]

D.  [INSERT: The Bank is willing to enter into this Agreement on the terms and conditions set forth herein.]

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1.  DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1  Definitions.  Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them in the Credit Agreement or the Security Agreement, as applicable.  As used in this Agreement:

“Account” means each deposit account identified on Schedule A hereto (as Schedule A may be amended or supplemented from time to time by written agreement of the parties), [INSERT: together with any renewal, replacement, substitute, renumbered, or successor account, and any sub-account, linked account, or concentration account related thereto], maintained by the Company with the Bank, [INSERT: including all monies, checks, securities entitlements, financial assets, instruments, and other property from time to time deposited in, credited to, or held in such account(s)].

[INSERT: “Account Collateral” has the meaning set forth in the Recitals.]

[INSERT: “Business Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York [INSERT: or in the city in which the office of the Bank at which the Account is maintained is located] are authorized or required by law to close.]

[DELETE: “Control” means the Bank will follow the Company’s instructions unless the Secured Party says otherwise.]
[INSERT: “Control” has the meaning set forth in Section 9-104 of the UCC (and, to the extent applicable to any securities entitlement or commodity contract credited to the Account, Sections 9-106 and 9-314 of the UCC).]

[INSERT: “Entitlement Order” has the meaning set forth in Section 8-102(a)(8) of the UCC.]

[INSERT: “Instructions” means entitlement orders, instructions, notifications, or directions with respect to the disposition of funds or other property in the Account, including wire transfer instructions, ACH instructions, checks, and other payment orders.]

[INSERT: “Notice of Exclusive Control” or “NOEC” means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A hereto (or such other form as the Bank and Secured Party may agree), stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Account.]

[INSERT: “Secured Obligations” means all “Obligations” as defined in the Credit Agreement and all other obligations secured by the Security Agreement, whether now existing or hereafter arising.]

[INSERT: “Secured Parties” has the meaning set forth in the Credit Agreement.]

[DELETE: “Termination Date” means the date the Company pays the Bank’s fees.]
[INSERT: “Termination Date” means the date on which the Secured Party delivers to the Bank a written notice stating that (a) all Secured Obligations have been indefeasibly paid in full in cash, (b) all commitments under the Credit Agreement have terminated, and (c) the security interest of the Secured Party in the Account has been released (or such earlier date as the Secured Party may specify in a written release).]

1.2  UCC Terms.  Terms defined in Articles 8 or 9 of the UCC and not otherwise defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them therein.  [INSERT: The term “deposit account” has the meaning set forth in Section 9-102(a)(29) of the UCC.]

1.3  Rules of Construction.  [INSERT: The words “include,” “includes,” and “including” shall be deemed to be followed by the phrase “without limitation.”  References to “Sections,” “Schedules,” and “Exhibits” are to this Agreement unless otherwise indicated.  Headings are for convenience only and shall not affect interpretation.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2.  THE ACCOUNT; ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SECURITY INTEREST
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1  Identification of Account.  The Bank confirms that the Company is the Bank’s customer with respect to the Account identified on Schedule A.  [INSERT: The Bank shall not change the account number, title, or location of the Account, or convert the Account to any other type of account, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party, except for changes required by applicable law or the Bank’s automated systems that do not impair control, of which the Bank shall promptly notify the Secured Party.]

2.2  Security Interest.  The Company hereby confirms that it has granted [INSERT: (and hereby grants, to the extent not previously granted)] to the Secured Party, for the benefit of the Secured Parties, a security interest in the Account and the Account Collateral to secure the Secured Obligations.  [INSERT: The Bank acknowledges the security interest of the Secured Party in the Account and the Account Collateral.  The Bank has not received notice of any other adverse claim to, or security interest, lien, or encumbrance on, the Account or Account Collateral (other than the Bank’s rights expressly permitted under Section 4).]

2.3  [DELETE: The Bank may commingle the Account with other accounts.]
     [INSERT: Segregation; No Commingling Impairment.  Nothing in this Agreement requires the Bank to segregate physically the funds in the Account from other funds of the Bank; provided that the Bank’s books and records shall at all times identify the Account as subject to this Agreement and the Secured Party’s security interest.  The Bank shall not enter into any other control agreement, three-party agreement, or similar arrangement with respect to the Account with any person other than the Secured Party without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.]

2.4  [INSERT: Additional Accounts.  If the Company opens any additional deposit account with the Bank that is required to be subject to a control agreement under the Credit Agreement or Security Agreement, the Company and the Bank shall, upon request of the Secured Party, promptly execute and deliver a joinder or amendment to this Agreement (or a new control agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party) covering such account, and Schedule A shall be deemed amended accordingly.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3.  CONTROL; PRIORITY OF INSTRUCTIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1  Control.  [DELETE: The Bank will use commercially reasonable efforts to follow instructions from the Secured Party after notice.]
     [INSERT: The Bank agrees that it will comply with Instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of the funds in the Account without further consent by the Company.  The foregoing agreement by the Bank is intended to, and does, confer “control” upon the Secured Party within the meaning of Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC (and, as applicable, Section 9-106 of the UCC).  The Bank hereby subordinates any conflicting claim or right it may have, other than as expressly set forth in Section 4, to the security interest and control rights of the Secured Party.]

3.2  Pre-NOEC Operation (Springing Control).  [DELETE: The Company alone may operate the Account at all times until the loan is accelerated.]
     [INSERT: Until the Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control from the Secured Party:
     (a) the Bank may comply with Instructions originated by the Company (or its authorized representatives) with respect to the Account, including Instructions for withdrawal, payment, transfer, or other disposition of funds;
     (b) the Secured Party may, at any time, deliver Instructions to the Bank with respect to the Account, and the Bank shall comply with such Instructions without further consent of the Company; and
     (c) if the Bank receives conflicting Instructions from the Company and the Secured Party, the Bank shall comply with the Instructions of the Secured Party and shall have no liability to the Company for doing so.
     [COMMENT: Playbook requires true springing control with Secured Party override even pre-NOEC; counterparty draft’s “Company exclusive until acceleration” is rejected.]]

3.3  Notice of Exclusive Control.  [DELETE: Secured Party may send a notice of exclusive control only after an Event of Default that has continued for 30 days, and only with 10 Business Days’ prior written notice to the Company.]
     [INSERT: The Secured Party may deliver a Notice of Exclusive Control to the Bank at any time in its sole discretion (including, without limitation, upon or after the occurrence of an Event of Default under the Credit Agreement, but without any requirement that an Event of Default exist, continue, or be declared, and without any requirement of prior notice to or consent of the Company).  The Bank shall have no duty to inquire whether an Event of Default exists or whether the Secured Party is entitled under the Credit Agreement or otherwise to deliver a NOEC.]

3.4  Post-NOEC Exclusive Control.  [DELETE: After NOEC, Bank will endeavor to follow Secured Party instructions within a reasonable time, not to exceed five Business Days.]
     [INSERT: After the Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control:
     (a) the Bank shall cease complying with Instructions originated by the Company with respect to the Account and shall comply solely with Instructions originated by the Secured Party;
     (b) the Bank shall comply with Secured Party Instructions [INSERT: by the close of the Business Day of receipt if received before 12:00 noon (local time at the Bank’s office where the Account is maintained), or otherwise by the close of the next Business Day] (or such shorter period as may be required for same-day wires if operationally feasible);
     (c) the Company irrevocably authorizes and directs the Bank to comply exclusively with the Secured Party’s Instructions following NOEC; and
     (d) the Bank shall have no liability to the Company for complying with Secured Party Instructions after NOEC or for refusing Company Instructions after NOEC.]

3.5  [INSERT: Form and Delivery of NOEC and Instructions.  A Notice of Exclusive Control and any Instructions from the Secured Party shall be in writing (including email or other electronic transmission reasonably acceptable to the Bank) and delivered in accordance with Section 10.  The Bank may rely on any NOEC or Instruction that it reasonably believes in good faith to have been given by an authorized person of the Secured Party.  The Bank shall be entitled to rely upon any NOEC until the Bank receives a written rescission or release from the Secured Party.]

3.6  [INSERT: Rescission of NOEC.  The Secured Party may rescind a Notice of Exclusive Control by written notice to the Bank.  Upon receipt of such rescission, the Account shall again be operated in accordance with Section 3.2 until any subsequent NOEC.]

3.7  [DELETE: The Company may revoke this Agreement or the Secured Party’s control rights upon 30 days’ notice.]
     [INSERT: Irrevocability.  The Company may not terminate, amend, or revoke this Agreement, or the Secured Party’s control rights hereunder, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.  Any attempted termination, amendment, or revocation by the Company without such consent is void.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 4.  BANK’S RIGHTS; SUBORDINATION OF LIENS AND SETOFF
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1  [DELETE: Bank retains all rights of setoff, banker’s lien, and recoupment against the Account for any obligations of the Company to the Bank, whether now existing or hereafter arising, including reciprocal deposit arrangements and multi-lateral netting.]
     [INSERT: Limited Bank Liens; Subordination.
     (a) The Bank hereby waives, releases, and subordinates in favor of the Secured Party any security interest, lien, right of setoff, right of recoupment, banker’s lien, or other right or claim the Bank may have in or against the Account or Account Collateral, whether arising by agreement, operation of law, or otherwise, except solely for the following (collectively, the “Permitted Bank Claims”), which shall have priority over the Secured Party’s security interest solely to the extent described below:
         (i)  the Bank’s right to payment of its customary fees and charges for the maintenance and operation of the Account, as disclosed in the Bank’s applicable fee schedule (as in effect from time to time and provided to the Company and, upon request, to the Secured Party);
         (ii) the Bank’s right to reverse or charge back returned items, provisional credits, and corrections of posting errors with respect to the Account, in accordance with the Bank’s standard account documentation and applicable law; and
         (iii) [OPTIONAL IF PLAYBOOK PERMITS NARROW OVERDRAFT: the Bank’s right to reimbursement for overdrafts on the Account created in the ordinary course, not to exceed $[●] in the aggregate at any time, which right shall be limited to amounts advanced by the Bank to cover items presented against the Account]; provided that the Bank shall not permit habitual or material overdrafts and shall promptly notify the Secured Party of any overdraft remaining outstanding for more than [two (2)] Business Days.
     (b) Without limiting the foregoing, the Bank subordinates to the security interest of the Secured Party any right of setoff or banker’s lien arising from (i) loans, credit facilities, or other extensions of credit by the Bank (or its affiliates) to the Company or any affiliate of the Company, (ii) reciprocal account or cash-management arrangements not solely related to the operation of the Account, (iii) multi-lateral or bilateral netting arrangements, and (iv) any other obligations of the Company to the Bank other than the Permitted Bank Claims.
     (c) The Bank shall not exercise any Permitted Bank Claim in a manner that would prevent the Secured Party from receiving funds pursuant to a valid Instruction or NOEC, except to the extent necessary to satisfy then-due Permitted Bank Claims as expressly permitted above.]

4.2  [DELETE: Bank may freeze the Account at any time in its discretion for compliance or risk reasons without notice.]
     [INSERT: Account Freezes / Legal Process.  If the Bank receives a levy, attachment, garnishment, restraining order, or other legal process with respect to the Account, or if the Bank is required by law or regulation (including AML/sanctions screening) to freeze or restrict the Account, the Bank shall (a) to the extent legally permitted, promptly notify the Secured Party and the Company, (b) not voluntarily take any action that prefers other creditors over the Secured Party, and (c) interplead funds or otherwise act in a manner consistent with the Secured Party’s perfected security interest by control, to the maximum extent permitted by law.  The Bank’s compliance with legal process shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement.]

4.3  [INSERT: No Other Agreements.  The Bank represents that it has not entered into, and covenants that it will not enter into, any agreement with any third party (other than the Secured Party) by which the Bank is obligated to comply with Instructions originated by such third party concerning the Account.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 5.  REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1  Company Representations.  The Company represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank that:
     (a)  it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization;
     (b)  it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
     (c)  this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered by it and constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms;
     (d)  [INSERT: it is the sole owner of the Account and the Account Collateral, free and clear of all liens other than the security interest of the Secured Party and Permitted Bank Claims];
     (e)  [INSERT: the Account is a “deposit account” as defined in Section 9-102(a)(29) of the UCC, and the Bank is a “bank” as defined in Section 9-102(a)(8) of the UCC];
     (f)  [INSERT: the Account is not a “securities account” or “commodity account” within the meaning of the UCC; provided that if any financial assets are at any time credited to the Account, the control provisions of this Agreement shall apply mutatis mutandis under UCC §§ 9-106 and 8-106]; and
     (g)  [INSERT: execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with its organizational documents, any material agreement binding on it, or any law or order applicable to it].

5.2  Bank Representations.  The Bank represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Company that:
     (a)  it is a [national banking association / state-chartered bank] duly organized and validly existing under the laws of [the United States / State of ●];
     (b)  it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
     (c)  this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered by it and constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation;
     (d)  [INSERT: it maintains the Account as a deposit account in the ordinary course of its banking business, and the State in which the office of the Bank that maintains the Account is located is [State] for purposes of UCC § 9-304];
     (e)  [INSERT: it has not entered into any currently effective agreement with any third party to comply with Instructions originated by such third party concerning the Account]; and
     (f)  [INSERT: the person executing this Agreement on behalf of the Bank is duly authorized to do so].

5.3  [INSERT: Secured Party Representation.  The Secured Party represents that it is authorized under the Credit Agreement to enter into this Agreement as Administrative Agent for the benefit of the Secured Parties.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 6.  COVENANTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1  Company Covenants.  The Company covenants that it shall:
     (a)  [INSERT: not permit any person other than the Secured Party and the Bank (as to Permitted Bank Claims only) to have “control” (as defined in the UCC) over the Account];
     (b)  [INSERT: not enter into any other control agreement or similar arrangement with respect to the Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party];
     (c)  [INSERT: not change the name or jurisdiction of organization of the Company, or the account name or number of the Account, without prior written notice to the Secured Party and the Bank and, in the case of account name/number changes, compliance with Section 2.1];
     (d)  [INSERT: maintain the Account as a deposit account at the Bank and not close the Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party, except upon transfer of all balances to another account subject to a control agreement in favor of the Secured Party in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party];
     (e)  [DELETE: provide monthly account statements only to the Company]
         [INSERT: authorize and direct the Bank to provide to the Secured Party, upon the Secured Party’s request, copies of account statements, transaction detail, balance information, and other information regarding the Account that the Bank customarily makes available to customers, and the Company hereby consents to such disclosure]; and
     (f)  [INSERT: execute and deliver such further documents and take such further actions as the Secured Party or the Bank may reasonably request to perfect, maintain, or enforce the Secured Party’s control and security interest].

6.2  Bank Covenants.  The Bank covenants that it shall:
     (a)  [INSERT: maintain the Account in accordance with this Agreement and its standard account documentation, except to the extent this Agreement expressly provides otherwise (in which case this Agreement controls)];
     (b)  [INSERT: not agree to comply with Instructions concerning the Account from any person other than the Company (prior to NOEC, subject to Section 3.2) and the Secured Party];
     (c)  [INSERT: upon request of the Secured Party from time to time, confirm in writing the account balance, account number, and that this Agreement remains in full force and effect];
     (d)  [INSERT: promptly (and in any event within two (2) Business Days) notify the Secured Party if the Bank receives notice of any adverse claim, lien, levy, or legal process against the Account, or if the Company seeks to close or transfer the Account]; and
     (e)  [DELETE: Bank may amend its deposit account agreement at any time without notice to Secured Party]
         [INSERT: not amend the underlying deposit account agreement or terms governing the Account in a manner that adversely affects the Secured Party’s rights under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Secured Party; provided that changes to the Bank’s generally applicable fee schedules and operational procedures that do not impair control or priority may be made in accordance with the Bank’s standard practices, with notice to the Company].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 7.  DUTIES AND STANDARD OF CARE OF THE BANK; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1  Duties.  [DELETE: The Bank’s only duty is to act in good faith; the Bank has no duties except those expressly set forth, and all fiduciary duties are disclaimed to the maximum extent permitted by law, including any duty of care.]
     [INSERT: The Bank undertakes to perform only such duties as are expressly set forth in this Agreement and no implied duties.  The Bank shall exercise the same care in performing its duties under this Agreement as it exercises with respect to similar accounts maintained for its other customers, [INSERT: and shall act in good faith and with ordinary care within the meaning of the UCC].  The Bank shall not be deemed to have any fiduciary duty to the Company or the Secured Party by reason of this Agreement.]

7.2  Limitation of Liability.  [DELETE: The Bank shall have no liability of any kind to any party under this Agreement, including for negligence, and the Company’s sole remedy is to close the Account.]
     [INSERT: The Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted to be taken by it under or in connection with this Agreement, except for the Bank’s own gross negligence or willful misconduct as determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.  In no event shall the Bank be liable for any special, indirect, consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages, whether or not advised of the possibility thereof, except to the extent resulting from the Bank’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.  The Bank shall have no liability for following Instructions (including a NOEC) that it reasonably believes to be genuine and authorized.]

7.3  [INSERT: Reliance.  The Bank may rely upon any notice, Instruction, NOEC, certificate, or other document believed by it in good faith to be genuine and to have been signed or sent by the proper person.  The Bank may consult with legal counsel and shall not be liable for action taken in good faith in accordance with the advice of such counsel.]

7.4  [INSERT: Force Majeure; Interruption of Services.  The Bank shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performance due to circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, government action, natural disaster, labor dispute, failure of utilities or communications, or failure of the Fedwire or other payment systems; provided that the Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance and shall notify the parties promptly of any material interruption affecting the Account.]

7.5  [INSERT: No Duty to Monitor Credit Agreement.  The Bank shall have no duty to monitor compliance by the Company with the Credit Agreement or any other document, to determine whether an Event of Default exists, or to investigate the right of the Secured Party to issue a NOEC or any Instruction.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
================================================================================
TO:       File; Transaction Working Group; Client ([Borrower] / Sponsor Counsel as applicable)
FROM:     Banking & Finance — Contracts / Collateral Counsel
DATE:     [Closing Timeline Date]
RE:       Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement against Internal
          Playbook, Executed Credit Agreement, Depository Bank Standard Form,
          Account Details, and Related Correspondence/Checklists
MATTER:   Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement
          Counterparty Paper
OUTPUTS:  aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline of draft ACA)
          issues-risk-memo.docx (this memorandum)
STATUS:   Counsel analysis complete; redline prepared for circulation to Bank
          and Company counsel

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We reviewed the counterparty’s draft Account Control Agreement (“Draft ACA”)
against: (i) the firm’s internal Account Control Agreement Playbook (v4.2)
(“Playbook”); (ii) the executed Credit Agreement and related Collateral
Documents (Guarantee and Collateral Agreement / Security Agreement)
(collectively, “CA”); (iii) the depository bank’s standard form ACA (“Bank
Form”); (iv) account opening details and the deposit-account diligence
checklist; and (v) related correspondence on springing control, Notice of
Exclusive Control (“NOEC”) mechanics, and post-closing control conditions.

The Draft ACA is materially off-market and does not establish reliable “control”
under NY UCC § 9-104 sufficient to perfect and prioritize the Secured Party’s
security interest on a first-priority basis, nor does it satisfy typical CA
conditions precedent / post-closing covenants requiring control agreements “in
form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.”

Principal defects fall into six clusters:

  1. Control mechanics that are conditional, delayed, or “commercially
     reasonable efforts”–based rather than an absolute Bank covenant to comply
     with Secured Party instructions (UCC § 9-104(a)(2) failure risk).
  2. NOEC triggers requiring Event of Default + cure periods + advance notice to
     Company — incompatible with springing control and CA enforcement timing.
  3. Unsubordinated Bank setoff / banker’s lien / reciprocal and affiliate
     claims that can prime or erode Collateral.
  4. Bank termination and automatic-termination mechanics that allow release of
     funds to the Company free of the lien.
  5. Missing operational architecture: no Schedule A account particulars, no
     NOEC form, inadequate notices, wrong governing law, assignability blocks on
     successor agent.
  6. Liability / indemnity package that over-protects the Bank (complete
     negligence shield) and under-protects / over-exposes the Agent.

We have prepared a full tracked-changes redline (aca-redline.docx) incorporating
all required modifications and insertions.  Items rated CRITICAL or HIGH are
mandatory for sign-off; MEDIUM items should be obtained in market negotiations;
LOW items are cleanup / best practice.

Bottom-line recommendation: Do not accept the Draft ACA.  Circulate the redline
as Agent’s mark.  If the Bank insists on Bank Form, map each Playbook mandatory
item onto Bank Form and escalate residual gaps (especially setoff subordination,
NOEC at-will, successor-agent assignment, and control covenant language).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II.  SCOPE, MATERIALS REVIEWED, AND METHODOLOGY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Materials Reviewed
    1. Counterparty draft Account Control Agreement (three-party form among
       Company, Secured Party, and Bank) — the “Draft ACA.”
    2. Internal ACA Playbook v4.2 (mandatory positions, preferred positions,
       fall-backs, and deal-status flags for investment-grade vs. leveraged).
    3. Executed Credit Agreement — relevant provisions including:
         • Collateral / “Collateral Documents” definition and scope
         • § 5.11 (or equivalent) — Deposit Accounts; Control Agreements
         • § 6.12 (or equivalent) — Further Assurances; Post-Closing
         • Event of Default and remedy provisions (§ 8.01 et seq.)
         • Agency provisions (successor Administrative Agent)
         • Governing law (New York)
         • Excluded Account definition and thresholds (if any)
    4. Guarantee and Collateral Agreement / Security Agreement — grant clause
       covering deposit accounts and supporting obligations for control.
    5. Depository Bank standard form ACA and related fee/account documentation
       (as available).
    6. Account details / opening checklist: legal name match, account number,
       account title, ABA, branch location / UCC § 9-304 jurisdiction, sweep
       links, Excluded Account analysis.
    7. Correspondence / checklists re: springing vs. blocked control, NOEC
       operational contacts, and CP / post-closing control deliverables.

B.  Methodology
    • Clause-by-clause comparison of Draft ACA to Playbook mandatory and
      preferred positions and to Bank Form.
    • CA conformity check: does the Draft ACA satisfy “control” and “form and
      substance satisfactory to Agent” requirements, and agency succession?
    • UCC perfection/priority analysis under NY UCC §§ 9-104, 9-304, 9-314,
      9-327 (and §§ 8-106 / 9-106 if securities-account risk).
    • Operational enforceability: timing of instruction compliance, NOEC
      delivery, conflict-of-instruction hierarchy, freeze/legal process.
    • Risk rating each deviation: Critical / High / Medium / Low.
    • Exposure analysis: perfection failure, priority loss, enforcement delay,
      leakage via setoff, agency friction, opinion / CP failure.
    • Recommended position: Require / Strongly Prefer / Prefer / Accept-as-is
      (none of the material items are Accept-as-is).
    • Summary Deviation Matrix (Section VII).

C.  Assumptions and Open Items
    • Party names, account numbers, and dates in the redline remain bracketed
      pending final account diligence confirmation against Bank books and
      organic documents (exact legal name).
    • Confirm whether any linked sweep vehicle is a money-market mutual fund or
      securities account requiring separate securities-account control language
      (redline § 13 is protective).
    • Confirm Excluded Account thresholds under the CA before finalizing
      Schedule A coverage.
    • If Bank Form is non-negotiable on certain operational SLA timings, document
      Playbook exception with client approval for any residual MEDIUM items only.
    • No tax, regulatory (margin, Reg W), or sanctions deep-dive beyond standard
      PATRIOT Act notice and freeze language — flag if Bank is foreign branch.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III.  LEGAL FRAMEWORK (BRIEF)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Perfection of a security interest in a deposit account as original collateral
is achieved only by “control” under UCC § 9-312(b)(1) and § 9-314.  Control
via three-party agreement requires that the bank agree to “comply with
instructions originated by the secured party directing disposition of the funds
in the deposit account without further consent by the debtor” (UCC
§ 9-104(a)(2)).  Soft obligations (“commercially reasonable efforts,” delayed
effectiveness, EOD preconditions to NOEC, Company consent remnants) create a
material risk that a court or subsequent creditor will argue control never
attached or was lost.

Priority among conflicting security interests in deposit accounts is governed
by UCC § 9-327: a secured party with control has priority over a secured party
that does not; timing of control and the bank’s own interests are critical.
Unsubordinated bank setoff and banker’s liens can prime or effectively erode
recoveries.  Choice-of-law for perfection and priority of deposit accounts is
determined by the bank’s jurisdiction under UCC § 9-304 — hence the need to
identify the office that maintains the Account and align governing-law and
notices provisions.

Market / Playbook baseline for leveraged and mid-market facilities:
  • Springing control (Company operates until NOEC; Agent may NOEC at will).
  • Absolute Bank covenant to comply with Agent instructions (pre- and
    post-NOEC hierarchy clear).
  • Broad subordination of Bank liens/setoff other than narrow Permitted Bank
    Claims (fees, chargebacks, sometimes limited ordinary-course overdrafts).
  • No Bank unilateral termination that dumps cash to Company; transition
    mechanics required.
  • Successor Administrative Agent takes by notice, not Bank consent.
  • NY law (if CA is NY), jury waiver, complete notice architecture, NOEC form
    exhibit, precise Schedule A.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV.  DETAILED ISSUES ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each issue below identifies: Draft ACA position → Playbook / CA / Bank Form
requirement → Risk rating → Exposure analysis → Recommended position → Redline
disposition (section reference in aca-redline.docx).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 1 — Absence of Absolute Control Covenant (UCC § 9-104(a)(2))
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Bank will use “commercially reasonable efforts” to follow Secured Party
  instructions “after notice,” with no express agreement to comply without
  further Company consent.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Bank “agrees that it will comply with instructions
  originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of the funds in the
  Account without further consent by the Company.”  CA requires control
  sufficient to perfect.  Bank Form typically contains hard comply language
  (sometimes with operational cut-off times).

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Exposure Analysis:
  Without a hard comply covenant, Secured Party may fail to obtain “control”
  under § 9-104(a)(2).  Consequences: unperfected security interest in the
  deposit account as original collateral; loss of § 9-327 priority; possible
  CP/post-closing default; unhelpful or qualified perfection opinion; in
  bankruptcy, vulnerability to competing liens and inadequate cash collateral
  position.  “Commercially reasonable efforts” is not a statutory substitute
  for the UCC control test.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE hard comply language; no “efforts” qualifier on
the control covenant itself.  Operational cut-offs (e.g., noon same-day / next
Business Day) are acceptable as timing mechanics, not as diligence qualifiers
on the duty to comply.

Redline Disposition: § 3.1 (rewrite); related §§ 3.2–3.4.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 2 — NOEC Conditioned on Event of Default + Cure + Advance Notice to Company
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Secured Party may deliver NOEC only after an Event of Default that has
  continued for 30 days, and only with 10 Business Days’ prior written notice
  to the Company.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory (leveraged / standard Agency): NOEC exercisable at any time
  in Secured Party’s sole discretion; Bank has no duty to verify EOD or CA
  entitlement.  CA remedies are immediate upon EOD (subject to any CA-level
  notice/cure, which must not be re-litigated inside the ACA).  Bank Form
  usually permits NOEC at will; Bank does not want to police EOD.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Exposure Analysis:
  Re-imposing EOD + 30-day continuance + 10 Business Day advance notice inside
  the ACA can delay exclusive control by 40+ days after default — during which
  Company can drain the Account.  Creates conflict with CA enforcement timeline
  and cash dominion expectations.  Also forces Bank into EOD fact-finding,
  which Banks reject and which injects uncertainty into control.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE NOEC at will; delete EOD precondition, cure, and
Company advance-notice requirements from the ACA.  Any commercial constraint on
when Agent “should” NOEC belongs in the CA/intercreditor dynamics, not the ACA.

Redline Disposition: § 3.3 (rewrite); Exhibit A (NOEC form).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 3 — Pre-NOEC “Company Exclusive” Operation; No Secured Party Override
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Company alone may operate the Account at all times until the loan is
  accelerated (or until NOEC under the defective trigger above).

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Springing control structure — Company may operate until
  NOEC, BUT Secured Party may give Instructions at any time pre-NOEC, and in
  case of conflict Bank complies with Secured Party.  True “blocked” control
  (Agent-only from day one) is acceptable if commercially agreed but not
  required; “Company exclusive with no Agent override” is not acceptable.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Exposure Analysis:
  If Agent cannot originate binding Instructions pre-NOEC, control under
  § 9-104(a)(2) is questionable even before considering the NOEC trigger
  defects.  The statute requires Bank agreement to comply with Secured Party
  instructions without further debtor consent — not merely after a future
  contingency.  Also impairs interim protective steps (partial holds, directed
  transfers) short of full exclusive control.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE springing control with Secured Party override and
conflict hierarchy favoring Secured Party (§ 3.2 structure in redline).

Redline Disposition: § 3.2; § 3.4 (post-NOEC exclusive).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 4 — Post-NOEC Compliance Timing (“Endeavor within 5 Business Days”)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  After NOEC, Bank will “endeavor” to follow Secured Party instructions within
  a “reasonable time, not to exceed five Business Days.”

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred / near-Mandatory: Hard obligation; same-day if received
  before stated cut-off (e.g., 12:00 noon local), otherwise next Business Day.
  “Endeavor” is unacceptable.  Five Business Days is off-market for cash
  dominion and wire execution.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  Five-Business-Day lag enables significant cash leakage post-default and is
  inconsistent with Fedwire / chaps same-day expectations.  “Endeavor”
  reintroduces efforts-based uncertainty into the core control performance.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE hard post-NOEC comply obligation with market
cut-off times (noon same-day / next Business Day).  Fall-back: next Business Day
without noon cut-off if Bank systems require; never longer than one Business Day
for standard wires without client-approved exception.

Redline Disposition: § 3.4(b).

ISSUE 5 — Company Unilateral Revocation / Termination Rights
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Company may revoke the Agreement or Secured Party’s control rights upon 30
  days’ notice.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Company may not terminate, amend, or revoke without
  Secured Party consent while Secured Obligations / commitments remain
  outstanding.  Control must be irrevocable as to debtor.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Exposure Analysis:
  Debtor-revocable control is not reliable control.  Priority and perfection
  can be destroyed at Company’s election — fatal in workout and bankruptcy
  planning.  Directly conflicts with Security Agreement grant and CA covenants.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE irrevocability as to Company; termination only on
Secured Party release / Termination Date mechanics.

Redline Disposition: § 3.7; § 9.5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 6 — Unsubordinated / Unlimited Bank Setoff, Banker’s Lien, Reciprocal and
          Multi-Lateral Netting Rights
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Bank retains all rights of setoff, banker’s lien, and recoupment against the
  Account for any obligations of the Company to the Bank, now existing or
  hereafter arising, including reciprocal deposit arrangements and multi-lateral
  netting.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Bank waives/subordinates all liens and setoff except
  narrow “Permitted Bank Claims” — (i) customary account fees/charges,
  (ii) returned items / chargebacks / posting corrections, and (iii) optionally
  limited ordinary-course overdrafts with cap and notice.  Express
  subordination of loan/credit-facility setoff, affiliate claims, reciprocal
  and multi-lateral netting not solely operational to the Account.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Exposure Analysis:
  Unsubordinated Bank claims can prime Agent under UCC § 9-327 and common-law
  setoff, enabling the Bank (often also a Lender or affiliate of a Lender) to
  absorb Account balances for unrelated exposures.  Multi-lateral netting and
  reciprocal arrangements are particularly opaque and can drain Controlled
  Account value overnight.  Material gap versus CA expectation of first-priority
  perfected security interest in deposit accounts.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE broad waiver/subordination with only narrow
Permitted Bank Claims.  If Bank insists on overdraft priority, cap it and add
prompt notice + no habitual overdraft covenant.  Reject reciprocal / multi-
lateral netting priority against the Account.

Redline Disposition: § 4.1 (full rewrite); conforming changes in §§ 2.2, 5.1.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 7 — Bank Discretionary Freeze Without Notice Framework
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Bank may freeze the Account at any time in its discretion for “compliance or
  risk reasons” without notice.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred: Freezes limited to legal process / law / regulation
  (AML, sanctions); prompt notice to Secured Party and Company to the extent
  legally permitted; no voluntary preference of other creditors over Secured
  Party; interpleader / consistent-with-lien conduct.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  Open-ended freeze rights create operational dead zones during enforcement and
  can be used to pressure commercial outcomes.  Lack of notice prevents Agent
  from seeking emergency relief or directing alternative cash management.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE law/legal-process limitation + prompt notice +
non-preference language.  Accept standard sanctions/AML freeze reservations.

Redline Disposition: § 4.2.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 8 — Missing Covenant Against Other Control Agreements / Third-Party
          Instruction Agreements
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Silent (no representation or covenant that Bank has not and will not agree to
  comply with a third party’s instructions regarding the Account).

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Bank represents no currently effective conflicting control
  agreement and covenants not to enter one; Company covenants not to grant
  others control.  Essential to § 9-104 exclusivity and § 9-327 priority.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  A second control agreement in favor of another creditor can create priority
  fights and operational paralysis (conflicting entitlement orders).  Silence
  is a diligence and enforcement gap.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE Bank rep + covenant (§§ 4.3, 5.2, 6.1, 6.2) and
Company negative control covenant.

Redline Disposition: §§ 2.3, 4.3, 5.2(e), 6.1(a)–(b), 6.2(b).

ISSUE 9 — Inadequate / Missing Account Identification (Schedule A)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Vague reference to “Company operating account at Bank” without account
  number, title, ABA, branch location, or UCC § 9-304 jurisdiction; no sweep /
  sub-account identification; no amendment mechanics.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Precise Schedule A — legal name, account title, number,
  type, currency, ABA, office location, Bank jurisdiction for § 9-304, sweeps.
  Joinder/amendment path for additional accounts required by CA.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL (as to perfection certainty) / HIGH (operational)

Exposure Analysis:
  Ambiguous account identification risks failure to attach control to the
  intended account, mismatch with Bank books, and exclusion of renumbered or
  successor accounts.  Sweep vehicles may be uncontrolled leakage paths.
  Opining counsel and CA CP checklists will reject vague schedules.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE completed Schedule A with all fields; add
successor/replacement account coverage and additional-account joinder.

Redline Disposition: Definition of “Account”; § 2.1; § 2.4; Schedule A.

ISSUE 10 — Automatic Termination; Bank Termination on 15 Days’ Notice with
           Payover to Company
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Agreement terminates automatically 90 days after the Credit Agreement “ends,”
  whether or not Bank receives notice; Bank may terminate on 15 days’ notice
  for any reason and upon termination may pay all funds to the Company.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Termination only upon Secured Party written release /
  Termination Date notice confirming indefeasible payment in full, commitment
  termination, and lien release (or earlier Secured Party election).  Bank
  termination only on longer notice (typically ≥30 days), with mandatory
  transfer per Secured Party Instructions (or interpleader) — never free
  payover to Company.  No automatic termination by CA sunset alone without
  Agent confirmation (refinancings, amendments, lingering contingent Obligations
  make “CA ends” indeterminate for Bank).

Risk Rating: CRITICAL

Exposure Analysis:
  Automatic termination and free payover to Company can destroy perfection at
  the worst moment (workout, liability management, residual contingent secured
  obligations, LC exposure).  Short Bank walk-away with payover is a structural
  hole in cash collateral.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE Agent-controlled Termination Date mechanics;
  rewrite Bank termination; prohibit payover to Company free of lien.

Redline Disposition: Definitions (“Termination Date”); §§ 9.1–9.5; Exhibit B.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 11 — Governing Law = Bank Branch State; No NY Alignment; No Jury Waiver /
           Forum
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Governed by laws of the State in which the Bank’s branch is located, without
  regard to UCC choice-of-law rules; no jury waiver; no exclusive forum.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory where CA is NY: NY governing law for the ACA contract,
  while recognizing UCC § 9-304 bank-jurisdiction rules for perfection/priority.
  Jury waiver and NY forum to match CA.

Risk Rating: HIGH (CRITICAL if branch-law conflicts with CA enforcement package
or creates multi-forum litigation risk on interlocking documents)

Exposure Analysis:
  Divergent governing law complicates enforcement with CA/Security Agreement,
  increases opinion complexity, and may produce inconsistent interpretations of
  control and indemnity provisions.  Omitting § 9-304 recognition confuses
  perfection analysis.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE NY law + § 9-304 savings language + jury waiver +
NY forum, matching CA.  Fall-back only if CA itself uses Bank’s local law and
client approves.

Redline Disposition: §§ 11.1–11.3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 12 — Anti-Assignment / Bank Consent Required for Successor Agent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Secured Party may not assign to a successor agent without Bank’s prior written
  consent (not to be unreasonably withheld); general anti-assignment.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Successor Administrative Agent under the CA takes Secured
  Party rights under the ACA by notice, without Bank or Company consent.
  Aligns with CA agency succession provisions.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  Bank consent gates on agent succession create leverage at resignation/
  removal and can delay enforcement continuity.  Off-market versus LSTA-style
  agency mechanics.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE assignment to successor Agent by notice only;
  limit Bank assignment to merger / deposit-business sale with assumption.

Redline Disposition: § 12.3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 13 — Amendments Without Secured Party Consent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Company and Bank may amend without Secured Party consent if amendment does
  not “materially” adversely affect Secured Party.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: All amendments require written agreement of Company, Bank,
  and Secured Party.  “Materiality” qualifier is subjective and invites dispute
  during distress.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  Unilateral Company/Bank amendments can erode control, expand Bank setoff, or
  alter instruction mechanics without Agent visibility.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE tri-party written amendments only.

Redline Disposition: § 12.2; conflict rule in § 12.1 (ACA controls over deposit
terms as among parties).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 14 — Bank Standard of Care / Complete Negligence Shield
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Bank’s only duty is “good faith”; all fiduciary duties disclaimed; Bank has
  “no liability of any kind,” including for negligence; Company’s sole remedy
  is to close the Account.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred / market: Express duties only; ordinary care / same care as
  for similar customer accounts; liability carve-out for Bank’s gross negligence
  or willful misconduct (final judgment).  Complete negligence immunity and
  “sole remedy = close account” are off-market and can hollow out the control
  covenant.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  If Bank faces no realistic liability for failing to comply with Agent
  instructions, the control covenant’s practical value is diminished and
  damages for misfires (wrong payee, ignored NOEC) may be unavailable.
  Opposing counsel sometimes accepts gross-negligence standard; simple-
  negligence liability is harder against large banks but complete immunity
  should be rejected.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE gross negligence / willful misconduct carve-out
from liability limitations; delete “sole remedy is close the Account.”  Accept
no-fiduciary-duty and no-consequential-damages (subject to GN/WM carve-out).

Redline Disposition: §§ 7.1–7.5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 15 — Indemnity Package (Company Too Narrow; Agent Over-Exposed;
           Missing Survival)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Company indemnifies Bank only for third-party claims arising from Company’s
  gross negligence; each party bears its own costs; no indemnity path for Bank
  failure affecting Secured Party; silent on Agent indemnity and survival.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory/Preferred: Broad Company indemnity to Bank (except Bank
  GN/WM); limited Agent indemnity only for losses from Bank’s compliance with
  Agent Instructions/NOEC, capped by amounts actually recovered from
  Company/Collateral (no full recourse to Agent’s own funds); Company pays
  Bank’s reasonable documented enforcement/negotiation expenses; survival of
  indemnity.

Risk Rating: HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  Narrow Company indemnity is non-starters for Banks and will stall execution.
  Conversely, uncapped full-recourse Agent indemnity is off-market for agency
  roles and can create unexpected balance-sheet exposure for the Agent bank.
  Missing expense coverage causes friction on every amendment and enforcement
  step.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE broad Company→Bank indemnity (GN/WM carve-out);
  limited recovery-based Agent→Bank indemnity; Company expense coverage;
  survival.

Redline Disposition: §§ 8.1–8.4.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 16 — Notices (Oral / “Effective When Sent”; No Authorized-Person Framework)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Notices may be oral or by any electronic means and are effective when sent;
  no specimen/authority framework for NOEC or Instructions.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Mandatory: Written notices; specified delivery methods and receipt
  conventions; email permitted with parameters; authorized-person / distribution
  list mechanics for Instructions and NOEC; Bank entitlement to rely on good-
  faith belief of authority.

Risk Rating: MEDIUM-HIGH

Exposure Analysis:
  Oral NOEC/Instructions create proof problems and fraud risk.  “Effective when
  sent” without receipt conventions causes disputes about when exclusive control
  began.  Banks will demand authority certificates; better to pre-wire balanced
  mechanics than fight operational refusals later.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE written notices + receipt rules + authority
framework; allow email.

Redline Disposition: §§ 3.5, 10.1–10.2; Schedule B.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 17 — Missing Recitals / Credit Agreement and Security Agreement Cross-Wire
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Minimal recitals (“Company maintains accounts; parties desire to enter
  agreement”); no CA or Security Agreement reference; no statement of purpose
  to perfect by control; Secured Party capacity unclear.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred / documentary integrity: Recitals reference CA, Security
  Agreement grant, perfection-by-control purpose, and Agent capacity for ratable
  benefit of Secured Parties.  Supports interpretation, estoppel, and opinion
  narratives.

Risk Rating: MEDIUM

Exposure Analysis:
  Weak context invites arguments that ACA is a mere service agreement rather
  than a control/perfection instrument; muddies third-party beneficiary status
  of Secured Parties.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE expanded recitals and Agent capacity language
(as in redline preamble and Recitals A–D).

Redline Disposition: Preamble; Recitals A–D; § 5.3; § 12.6.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 18 — Missing / Weak Company and Bank Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Sparse or missing reps on ownership of Account, deposit-account character,
  Bank status, no conflicting control agreements, authorization, and § 9-304
  location.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred: Standard corporate authority reps; Company ownership and
  deposit-account character; Bank organization, authorization, no conflicting
  agreements, office location / jurisdiction.

Risk Rating: MEDIUM

Exposure Analysis:
  Gaps impair diligence reliance and can complicate opinions and enforcement
  narratives.  Mis-characterization risk if Account is or becomes a securities

Recommended Position: REQUIRE expanded § 5 package; add protective § 13 if
financial assets may be credited.

Redline Disposition: §§ 5.1–5.3; § 13.

ISSUE 19 — Information Rights / Statements to Secured Party
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Monthly statements only to Company; no Secured Party information rights.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred / often Mandatory on Agency deals: Company authorizes Bank
  to deliver statements, balances, and transaction detail to Secured Party on
  request; Bank confirms Agreement in force on request.

Risk Rating: MEDIUM

Exposure Analysis:
  Without visibility, Agent cannot police cash dominion, detect leakage, or
  prepare enforcement.  CA reporting covenants are weaker substitutes for
  direct Bank feeds.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE Company authorization + Bank covenant to provide
information and periodic confirmation.

Redline Disposition: §§ 6.1(e), 6.2(c)–(d).

ISSUE 20 — Bank May Freely Amend Deposit Account Terms Adverse to Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Bank may amend its deposit account agreement at any time without notice to
  Secured Party.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred: No amendment of underlying deposit terms that adversely
  affects Secured Party rights without Secured Party consent; ACA controls over
  deposit terms on conflicts among the parties.  Ordinary fee schedule changes
  OK with notice.

Risk Rating: MEDIUM

Exposure Analysis:
  Adverse amendments (e.g., expanding setoff, changing instruction
  authentication in ways that block Agent) can silently impair control.

Recommended Position: REQUIRE adverse-amendment consent + ACA-prevails clause.

Redline Disposition: §§ 6.2(e), 12.1.

ISSUE 21 — Confidentiality Too Loose
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft ACA Position:
  Bank may disclose Agreement and account information to any affiliate, service
  provider, or prospective assignee freely.

Playbook / CA / Bank Form Requirement:
  Playbook Preferred: Need-to-know + confidentiality stream; regulatory/legal
  process exception; Agent may share with Lenders/assignees/participants per CA.

Risk Rating: LOW-MEDIUM

Exposure Analysis:
  Primarily commercial/privacy concern; limited perfection impact.

Recommended Position: PREFER tightened confidentiality (§ 12.10 redline).

ISSUE 22 — Missing NOEC Form, Termination/Release Form, Signature Authority

  Playbook Preferred / operational Mandatory: Agreed NOEC form exhibit reduces

Risk Rating: MEDIUM (operational CRITICAL at enforcement time if omitted)

  Playbook / CA: ACA delivery and actual control are typically CPs or

Risk Rating: HIGH (transactional)

  Executing a defective ACA can create a false “CP satisfied” record while

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

V.  ACCOUNT DILIGENCE & CHECKLIST GAPS (NON-DOCUMENTARY)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following diligence items must be completed or confirmed in parallel with
redline negotiation.  Failures here are as dangerous as documentary defects.

  D-1  Exact legal name of Company on Bank records matches CA / organic docs /
       UCC-1 debtor name (amend if mismatch).
  D-2  Account number, title, type, currency, open date verified by Bank
       callback or bank-stamped schedule — not solely Company email.
  D-3  Identify office that “maintains” the Account → UCC § 9-304 jurisdiction.
  D-4  Sweep, concentration, and sub-account map; control or exclude each leg.
  D-5  Existing control agreements, pledges, or multi-party deposit arrangements
       — obtain termination/release or subordination.
  D-6  Bank internal blocks, holds, or funded overdraft facilities.
  D-7  Authorized signers on Account vs. persons to be authorized for ACA
       Instructions (Company side) and Agent side specimen list.
  D-8  Fee schedule and any minimum-balance or compensating-balance arrangement
       that could function like a hidden Bank preference.
  D-9  Sanctions/AML status; any existing freezes.
  D-10 CA Excluded Account thresholds (e.g., payroll, petty cash, foreign)
       reconciled to Schedule A.
  D-11 Whether Bank is also a Lender / Arranger — manage affiliate setoff
       optics and ensure § 4.1 subordination still binds.
  D-12 Opinion coverage: will local counsel / NY counsel give control perfection
       opinion on this form?  If not, cure documentary gaps first.

VI.  RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION STRATEGY & ACTION PLAN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Circulate aca-redline.docx as Agent’s responsive mark with this memorandum
    as the issues list.  State that CRITICAL/HIGH items are conditions to
    accepting the ACA as a CA Collateral Document.

2.  If Bank refuses third-party paper and insists on Bank Form:
    (a) populate Bank Form with Playbook-required elections;
    (b) add a short negotiated rider covering: hard control covenant; NOEC at
        will + form; Permitted Bank Claims–only setoff; successor Agent by
        notice; termination/release mechanics; NY law if feasible; information
        rights;
    (c) escalate any residual CRITICAL gap to client with written risk
        acceptance request (do not silently accept).

3.  Parallel track: complete Section V diligence; freeze Schedule A only after
    Bank-side verification.

4.  Align with Agency / ops on NOEC contacts, email distribution lists, and
    after-hours protocols before closing.

5.  Confirm with CA drafting team that:
    • Collateral Documents definition picks up the ACA;
    • CP or post-closing schedule lists “control agreements in form and
      substance satisfactory to Agent, duly executed and delivered, establishing
      control”;
    • no CA provision inadvertently re-imposes EOD conditions on deposit-account
      remedies that would conflict with ACA NOEC-at-will (CA may still govern
      when Agent “should” exercise remedies as among Lenders/Borrower).

6.  Opinion / closing checklist: do not tick “deposit account control complete”
    until (i) redline CRITICAL items accepted, (ii) Schedule A finalized,
    (iii) fully executed counterparts received, and (iv) Bank ops acknowledges
    the ACA is loaded on the account (some banks require internal setup beyond
    signature).

7.  Fall-backs requiring express client approval if Bank is immovable:
    • Overdraft Permitted Bank Claim with low dollar cap + notice (Issue 6).
    • Next-Business-Day (no noon cut-off) post-NOEC wires (Issue 4).
    • Gross-negligence standard without simple-negligence exposure (Issue 14)
      — already our primary position.
    • Local Bank-branch governing law ONLY if CA is conformed and § 9-304 is
      clear (Issue 11) — disfavored.

8.  Items not to trade away without restructuring the facility’s cash-collateral
    thesis: Issues 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12 (CRITICAL/HIGH core).
